description: Merhaba! Biz KERKENEZLER takımı olarak NASA Space Apps Challenge kapsamında "Space Mission Design Game" projesi üzerinde çalışıyoruz. Amacımız hem eğlenceli hem de bilimsel olarak tutarlı bir uzay görevi tasarım oyunu geliştirmek. Şu anda kodlama, oyun tasarımı ve görsel/grafik tasarım konularında heyecanımıza ortak olacak, ekip çalışmasına yatkın yeni takım arkadaşları arıyoruz. Eğer sen de uzay keşfine ve oyun geliştirmeye meraklıysan, aramıza katıl!
summary:
First Colony on Mars is an interactive 3D web game where players establish and sustain a colony for three astronauts. The mission connects an Earth launch, interplanetary travel, Mars orbit, atmospheric entry, and surface operations.

Players explore a habitat, greenhouse, solar farm, battery storage, water plant, and oxygen production facility. A management tablet displays resources and facility controls, showing how power, water, oxygen, and crew survival depend on one another. An autonomous rover supports exploration and simulated science activities.

The colony uses solar power and batteries, extracts water from ice, recycles wastewater, and produces oxygen from atmospheric carbon dioxide through MOXIE inspired technology. Wheat and algae illustrate potential biological support, while their estimated output is distinguished from validated measurements. Nighttime and dust storms challenge players to balance energy supply and essential needs.

Built with JavaScript and Three.js, the game uses NASA references for mission physics, environmental conditions, crew consumption, and technology explanations. Conceptual hardware and simplified processes are identified as game assumptions.

The project makes Mars settlement challenges accessible through exploration, resource management, and visible consequences. It encourages scientific curiosity, systems thinking, and informed decisions about sustaining human life beyond Earth
details:
The experience begins with astronaut selection and progresses through Earth launch, interplanetary transfer, Mars orbital insertion, atmospheric entry, and landing. Flight data carries the crew, remaining supplies, and available modules into the colony, connecting both stages of the mission.

On the surface, players explore a habitat, greenhouse, solar farm, battery installation, water facility, and oxygen production plant. Airlocks provide controlled access to pressurized structures. A management tablet brings together facility controls, resource reserves, production readings, and energy information.

Colony systems

Solar panels generate electricity, while batteries store energy for periods without sufficient sunlight. Nighttime and dust storms constrain the power available to facilities, making resource management part of the challenge.

The water system models extraction from icy material and wastewater recovery. The oxygen facility uses MOXIE inspired technology to convert atmospheric carbon dioxide into oxygen, with carbon monoxide as a byproduct. The current design represents three banks of nine modules, using a reference production rate of six grams of oxygen per hour per module.

The greenhouse contains wheat and algae systems, irrigation, and supplemental purple lighting. Biological oxygen production is presented as an estimate based on stated assumptions, rather than a validated life support capability.

An autonomous rover explores the surrounding terrain and performs simulated scientific investigations. Players can monitor its status, recall it to base, and cancel the recall to resume its previous activity.

Scientific foundation and implementation

The game is built with JavaScript, Three.js, and Vite. NASA references inform flight physics, Martian environmental conditions, crew consumption, and technology explanations. NASA visual assets and procedural models support the environment.

We distinguish measured reference data from simplified calculations and conceptual hardware. The game is an educational simulation, not a validated engineering design or a guarantee that the modeled colony could sustain people on Mars.

Purpose and impact

Our goal is to make the challenges of human exploration understandable through decisions and visible consequences. Players can see how reduced electricity affects production, how reserves support survival, and why a settlement needs coordinated systems. By connecting a space journey with daily surface operations, the project encourages scientific curiosity, systems thinking, and informed discussion about sustainable human exploration beyond Earth.
